skill.description: Plan weekly work and manage Zentao tasks through preview-first scripts for listing, creating, completing, closing, and repairing task records.

skill.author: ariesyb

security_audit.summary: Most static alerts are false positives caused by Markdown formatting, Chinese text entropy, local configuration documentation, and ordinary Zentao identifier parsing. The client has two confirmed transport risks: it permits plaintext HTTP and does not enforce its origin boundary across redirects.

remediation.issue: Zentao credentials may be sent over plaintext HTTP.
remediation.suggestion: Require an HTTPS base URL, with an explicit local-development exception that never accepts production credentials.

remediation.issue: Automatic redirects are not checked against the configured Zentao origin.
remediation.suggestion: Disable redirects for authenticated requests or validate every redirect target by parsed scheme, hostname, port, and path before following it.

semantic_findings.title: Plain HTTP Can Expose Zentao Credentials
semantic_findings.description: The client accepts HTTP base URLs, then submits the Zentao account and password to the login endpoint without transport encryption.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The scheme check explicitly permits http://, and the login method directly posts both credential fields to that configured origin.

semantic_findings.title: Redirects Can Bypass the Configured Network Boundary
semantic_findings.description: Requests follows redirects by default, but the client validates only the initial URL. A cross-origin redirect can leave the configured Zentao origin.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The initial URL receives a prefix check, while the session request does not disable redirects or validate the final response URL and redirect history.

content.value_statement: Weekly planning often produces inconsistent tasks and manual Zentao updates. This skill structures schedules and previews supported task operations before execution.
actual_capabilities: Calculates current or next workdays with Chinese holiday support.
Builds standardized task plans with names, types, hours, and dates.
Lists active, assigned, finished, or closed Zentao tasks.
Previews and creates tasks from validated tabular plans.
Previews and completes or closes matching task groups.
Repairs task completion dates and historical effort dates.
limitations: Requires a reachable Zentao instance and user-provided credentials.
The current client accepts HTTP base URLs, which can expose credentials.
Task operations depend on the supported Zentao pages and response formats.
Write operations still require careful review before using the execute flag.

use_cases.title: Prepare a Weekly Plan
use_cases.description: Turn requirements and available workdays into a balanced task schedule with consistent fields.

use_cases.title: Review Team Workloads
use_cases.description: List assigned tasks and compare planned hours, dates, status, and remaining work.

use_cases.title: Maintain Zentao Records
use_cases.description: Preview task creation, completion, closure, or date repairs before approved execution.

prompt_templates.title: List My Tasks
prompt_templates.prompt: List my active Zentao tasks in a concise summary. Do not perform any write operation.

prompt_templates.title: Plan Next Week
prompt_templates.prompt: Plan my next workweek for requirement [ID]. Ask for missing details, use actual workdays, and keep each task between two and eight hours.

prompt_templates.title: Preview Task Creation
prompt_templates.prompt: Validate this task plan and preview the Zentao tasks that would be created. Report errors and wait for confirmation.

prompt_templates.title: Repair a Completion Date
prompt_templates.prompt: Preview repair of task [ID]. Show the deadline, affected effort records, assignee, and proposed changes without executing them.

output_examples.input: Plan next week for requirement 103615 with forty available hours.
output_examples.output: A dated work plan divides research, development, testing, and review into tasks between two and eight hours.

output_examples.input: Show my active tasks with common fields only.
output_examples.output: The summary lists each task identifier, name, status, priority, assignee, planned hours, consumed hours, remaining hours, and dates.
A preview lists the matched finished tasks and requests confirmation before any task is closed.

best_practices: Use HTTPS and provide credentials through protected process environment variables.
Review every preview and confirm task identifiers, dates, assignees, and hours.
Keep local credential files outside version control and skill packages.
anti_patterns: Do not execute a write operation without reviewing the preview.
Do not use plaintext HTTP for any Zentao account with real credentials.
Do not assume workdays, requirement identifiers, task types, or assignees.

faq.question: Does this skill create Zentao tasks automatically?
faq.answer: It previews validated tasks first. Actual creation requires the execute flag after user confirmation.

faq.question: Which credentials are required?
faq.answer: Provide the Zentao base URL, account, and password through process variables or an explicit local environment file.

faq.question: Can it plan around holidays?
faq.answer: Yes. It uses the Chinese calendar library when available and otherwise falls back to weekdays.

faq.question: Which task views can it list?
faq.answer: It supports active, assigned, finished, and closed task views exposed by the configured Zentao instance.

faq.question: Can it correct an incorrect completion date?
faq.answer: Yes. It previews activation and effort-date changes, then requires explicit execution.

faq.question: Does it send data to third-party services?
faq.answer: The code targets the configured Zentao site only, but redirect handling must be hardened before relying on that boundary.
